record.paper_title: A List of Problems on the Reverse Mathematics of Ramsey Theory on the Rado Graph and on Infinite, Finitely Branching Trees
record.original_question: Does the statement that the Halpern-Lauchli Theorem holds for any finite number of trees have the same reverse-mathematical strength as the statement that Milliken theorem for colorings of finite strong trees holds?

evidence.quote: Does “The Halpern-Läuchli Theorem holds for any finite number of trees” have the same strength as “Milliken’s Theorem for colorings of finite strong trees holds”?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Work within the framework of reverse mathematics over the base system RCA₀. Consider the following two combinatorial principles:

(HL) The Halpern–Läuchli theorem for any finite number of trees: For every positive integer d and every finite coloring of the level product ⋃_{n} (T_1(n) × ⋯ × T_d(n)) of d finitely-branching infinite trees T_1,…,T_d with no terminal nodes, there exist strong subtrees S_i ⊆ T_i (i = 1,…,d) sharing a common level set such that the induced level product is monochromatic.

(M_fst) Milliken's theorem for colorings of finite strong trees: For every finitely-branching infinite tree T with no terminal nodes, every positive integer k, and every finite coloring of the set of finite strong subtrees of T of size k, there exists an infinite strong subtree S ⊆ T all of whose finite strong subtrees of size k receive the same color. (A strong subtree is a subtree whose nodes lie on a common subset of levels of T and which is closed under taking immediate-successor branching of T.)

Question: Are the principles (HL) and (M_fst) equivalent over RCA₀? Equivalently, do they have the same reverse-mathematical strength?
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work by Anglès d'Auriac, Cholak, Dzhafarov, Monin, and Patey provides a comprehensive computability-theoretic classification of Milliken's tree theorem via an effective analysis of the Halpern–Läuchli theorem, but the available abstracts and summaries do not explicitly assert a proven RCA₀-equivalence between "Halpern–Läuchli for any finite number of trees" and "Milliken's theorem for colorings of finite strong trees." The exact reverse-mathematical equivalence appears not to be definitively settled in the sources surveyed.

status_evidence.title: Milliken's tree theorem and its applications: a computability-theoretic perspective
status_evidence.snippet: A careful analysis of the Halpern-Laüchli theorem shows that it can be carried out effectively, and this serves as the basis of a new inductive proof of Milliken's tree theorem that permits gauging its effectivity.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work analyzes both theorems together computability-theoretically, but the precise RCA₀-equivalence is not explicitly stated in available summaries.

status_evidence.title: The computational content of Milliken's tree theorem (Monin talk)
status_evidence.snippet: Talk on computability/reverse-math strength of Milliken's tree theorem via Halpern–Läuchli.
status_evidence.claim: Active research area; precise equivalence with Halpern–Läuchli for finite products not declared resolved.
